html:
The Khanate of Sibir was a state of the Siberian Tatars in western Siberia, along the Irtysh and Tobol rivers, from the late 1400s to 1598. It grew out of the break-up of the Golden Horde, and its capital was Qashliq, also called Isker, near today's Tobolsk. The whole of Siberia is named after it.

Two families descended from Genghis Khan, the Shaybanids and the Taibugids, fought over its throne. Its people were Turkic Tatars and Uralic forest peoples, who paid tribute in furs.

The Shaybanid Kuchum seized power in the 1560s, spread Islam, and stopped paying tribute to Muscovy. The rich Stroganov merchants of the Urals then hired a band of Cossacks under Yermak. In 1582 Yermak took Qashliq. He was killed in 1585, but Russian forts such as Tobolsk, founded in 1587, held the land. Kuchum fought on until his final defeat in 1598. The fall of Sibir opened the way for the Russian conquest of Siberia.
